data.source_title: Pathways to the emergency department - a national, cross-sectional study in Sweden
data.locator: Abstract; Results, pathway to ED and admission by pathway.
data.source_setting: Adult arrivals at 43 of Sweden’s 72 emergency departments; all patients present over an observed 24-hour period.
data.source_n: 3,875 adults overall; complete pathway data n=3,693; triage acuity recorded for n=3,365.
data.quantity: Observed pathway composition and admission share by arrival pathway
data.unit: patients; percent of pathway-complete sample or pathway subgroup
data.source_evidence_basis: National cross-sectional direct observation across 43 EDs: self-referred walk-in was the commonest pathway, followed by ambulance; ambulance arrivals had the highest admission rate.
data.limitations: One day, Sweden; nonrandom pathway groups differ in age and acuity. Does not specify registration or handoff durations, and admission proportions are not local arrival probabilities.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent arrival mode as an explicit branch into front-door workflows, with ambulance arrivals carrying a different acuity/admission mix only as an external scenario reference; do not assign RWJ rates from this study.
